vectors.cite: Initialization sequence figure, pdf 27; first instruction after reset runs, pdf 22
vectors.derivation: The initialization figure (pdf 27) starts counting at the MSYNC release: microcycle 0 is NACT, microcycle 1 is IAB (input starting program counter), microcycles 2 to 4 are NACT and the first BAR (output starting program counter) is in microcycle 5. So the reset entry unit is 5 cycles with one IAB access at offset 1. POL-RST-01: reset zero-fills R0-R7 and the status flags and clears INTFF; the IAB reply loads all 16 bits of R7, here the provider answers $0000 so R7 = $0000; R0-R6 stay 0 from the zero-fill (init values 1111..7777 are overwritten, status S and C and INTFF go from 1 to 0). The first instruction after the entry always runs (pdf 22), so prev_interruptible = 0. Run state goes RESET_PENDING -> RUNNING.

vectors.cite: Initialization sequence figure, pdf 27 (no IAB before MSYNC release)
vectors.derivation: POL-RST-01: a state that was never reset (all bytes zero, run state UNRESET) has not seen the MSYNC release that starts the initialization sequence (pdf 27), so the CPU has no program counter to fetch from. Stepping it reports a NOT_RESET unit of 0 cycles, makes no bus access and changes no state field.

vectors.cite: Control instructions table, CLRC row, pdf 56; instruction fetch figure, pdf 28
vectors.derivation: The control table (pdf 56) prints CLRC as 0000 000 110 = $0006, 4 cycles, 'CLeaR Carry to zero', marked Not Interruptable, with only C in the status change column. The instruction fetch figure (pdf 28) puts the BAR at cycle 0 and the DTB at cycle 2 of a 4-cycle fetch, so the whole instruction is the fetch: FETCH at cycle 0 from R7 = $1000, 4 cycles. One word is fetched, so R7 = $1000 + 1 = $1001. Not interruptible, so prev_interruptible = 0. R0-R6 are untouched. Init C = 1, S = Z = OV = 0: C becomes 0, S, Z and OV stay 0.

vectors.cite: Control instructions table, HLT row, pdf 56; instruction fetch figure, pdf 28; HALT pin, pdf 14
vectors.derivation: The control table (pdf 56) prints HLT as 0000 000 000 = $0000, 4 cycles, 'HaLT after next instruction is executed. Resume on control start.', with a blank status change column. One word is fetched, so R7 = $1000 + 1 = $1001. The halt is deferred to after the next instruction, so this unit only sets the stop latch: halt_pending 0 becomes 1, run state stays RUNNING and the event HALT_LATCHED is reported (POL-HLT-01, C40; the stop itself is evaluated at a later boundary, plan 02-15). The row is silent on interruptibility; the C56 default makes HLT non-interruptible, so prev_interruptible = 0 (init default 1). R0-R6 untouched. Init S = Z = OV = C = 1 all stay 1.

vectors.cite: Control instructions table, TCI row, pdf 56; TCI instruction timing figure, pdf 33
vectors.derivation: The control table (pdf 56) prints TCI as 0000 000 101 = $0005, 4 cycles, 'Terminate Current Interrupt. Not Interruptable.', with a blank status change column. The TCI instruction timing figure (pdf 33) shows BAR (cycle 0), NACT (1), DTB (2, input TCI instruction), NACT (3), then the BAR of the next instruction (cycle 4, output incremented program counter); the TCI pulse rises after t_TO in the NACT that follows that BAR, cycle 5. So the unit is 4 cycles with a FETCH at cycle 0 from R7 = $1000 and the STROBE_TCI record sits at unit end plus 1 = 4 + 1 = 5 (C39, D-12); a strobe carries no address or data, so addr = data = $0000. The event TCI is reported. One word is fetched, so R7 = $1001. Not interruptible, so prev_interruptible = 0 (init default 1). R0-R6 untouched. TCI drives only its pin: INTFF is not among the POL-INT-03 changes, so it keeps its init value. Init INTFF = 1 stays 1; init S = Z = OV = C = 1 all stay 1.

vectors.cite: Control instructions table, GSWD row, pdf 56; Fig 3.3.3 and footnote, pdf 51; instruction fetch figure, pdf 28
vectors.derivation: The control table (pdf 56) prints GSWD as 0000 110 0DD, 6 cycles, 'Get Status WorD in register DD. Bits 0-3, 8-11 set to 0. Bits 4, 12 = C; 5, 13 = OV; 6, 14 = Z; 7, 15 = S.', with a blank status change column; the pdf 51 footnote limits true GSWD to R0-R3. The instruction fetch figure (pdf 28) puts the BAR at cycle 0 and the DTB at cycle 2, so the only bus transfer is the FETCH at cycle 0 from R7 = $1000; the printed 6 cycles are the unit length. One word is fetched, so R7 = $1000 + 1 = $1001. The row carries no Not Interruptable note, so prev_interruptible becomes 1 (init 0). Status bits do not change. DD = 00 selects R0 ($0030). S = Z = OV = C = 1: bits 4-7 = 1111 gives $00F0 and bits 12-15 = 1111 gives $F000; bits 0-3 and 8-11 are 0. R0 = $00F0 + $F000 = $F0F0 (init $0001 overwritten). S, Z, OV, C stay 1.
